---
title: "Tree-based"
---

Tree-based models make predictions by repeatedly dividing the feature space
into smaller regions. Within each final region, a regression tree predicts an
average response and a classification tree predicts a class frequency.

## 1. Decision trees from scratch

**Estimated time:** 45–60 minutes

Build the first two splits of a high-CO decision tree from the gas-turbine
measurements. Compute Gini impurity, search across features and cutpoints, and
then use scikit-learn to draw the same shallow tree.

[View the notebook](01-decision-trees-from-scratch.ipynb)

## 2. How a decision tree grows

**Estimated time:** 5–10 minutes

Watch a simple two-feature classification tree add one conditional rule at a
time. See how each split creates a local decision region and the corresponding
decision process.

[Open the interactive animation](02-tree-growth-animation.qmd)

Use a small labeled dataset to see how a tree evaluates every available
cutpoint with weighted Gini impurity, then chooses the best one.

[Explore how a tree chooses a split](03-gini-split-explorer.qmd)

Watch a more mingled version of the mock data continue splitting until it
classifies every training observation correctly. See how a perfect training fit
can require increasingly local rules.

[Watch the overfitting animation](04-tree-overfitting-animation.qmd)
